domain_label: Movie Studio — Applied Audience Appeal Within the Likeness Boundary (Psych + Right-of-Publicity Law)
purpose: A method for the psychological-craft and legal-boundary judgments an expert reasons about when styling audience-appealing personas: which face/gaze/motion/body/styling cues the cited research actually supports (each carrying its FACT/ESTIMATE/contested tag), where Instagram's taste floor sits, and where the true right-of-publicity line falls -- identifiability by ANY cue, not just the face -- so that a celebrity-coded but wholly fictional aesthetic can be delivered without a specific real person ever becoming identifiable.
assumptions: no live A/B or engagement dataset is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior and every psychology/law claim is quoted from the grounding research file's FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags, not re-derived here

several primary sources (PMC5454066 gaze-cuing body, Meta's transparency.meta.com policy pages, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov article bodies) returned HTTP 403 through the egress proxy this session; those claims are carried at the downgraded confidence the grounding file assigned (indexed-summary or abstract-only), never upgraded to full-fetch FACT

contested findings (gaze-direction-to-product vs gaze-to-viewer, Singh's WHR 0.7 vs Tassinary & Hansen's confound critique and the Ugandan ~0.5 outlier, Frederick & Haselton's supra-normal-stimulus caveat) keep their contested/replication flags rather than being flattened into a single rule
the A4 practical-translation table and the A5 house rule are labeled [ESTIMATE] craft inference derived from the cited A1-A3 studies, never presented as measured fact

the likeness-boundary doctrine (Part B) is the load-bearing content of this KB: hiding the face does not neutralize identifiability, and no node in this KB may be read as guidance for evoking a specific real person while concealing the face -- that lane is closed and stated as closed
exclusions: the exact current verbatim Instagram/Meta policy thresholds for sexualized posing or implied nudity, which were proxy-blocked (403) this session and remain an explicit UNKNOWN the media-manager specialist must re-fetch before any borderline styling ships

guidance that would help maximize deniability while still evoking a specific real, living or dead person (the closed lane); this KB states the boundary and the safe fictional lane, it does not optimize around the boundary
the exact status of any federal 'NO FAKES'-style likeness statute as of the current date, which the grounding file marks UNKNOWN and does not verify
shot-by-shot cinematography, lighting, and camera-movement craft beyond the composition/attention cues this KB covers (belongs to the cinematography specialist)
brand/luxury prop sourcing and styling logistics beyond the status-cue psychology and the fictional-only hard constraint (belongs to the luxury/styling specialist)
invented engagement statistics, platform enforcement rates, or legal-case outcomes beyond what the grounding file's cited sources actually state

glossary.definition: The well-replicated eye-tracking finding that human faces attract gaze early in free-viewing and search tasks largely independent of task; Cerf, Frady & Koch (Journal of Vision, 2009) show a face-detection channel added to a bottom-up saliency model raises fixation-prediction AUC from ~0.53 to >0.84 on natural scenes [FACT], replicated on real-world stimuli (ACM ETRA 2020) [FACT].

The robust basic-attention phenomenon that observers shift attention toward where a depicted face looks [FACT]; its downstream effect on ad memory/purchase intent is CONTESTED -- Sajjacholapunt & Ball 2014 found averted gaze enhances outcomes while a ResearchGate eye-tracking study and D'Ambrogio et al. 2023 found gaze-to-product/celebrity-status interactions drive attention and purchase intent [FACT, contested]; the PMC5454066 gaze-cuing body was proxy-blocked (403) so its specific effect sizes are [UNKNOWN].

Singh (1993)'s proposed female-attractiveness cue (~0.7 WHR, moderate weight) [FACT], criticized by Tassinary & Hansen (1998) for confounding WHR with waist size/weight in the line-drawing stimuli, with cross-cultural replications mixed (one Ugandan sample preferring ~0.5 WHR and heavier weight) [FACT, contested]; 'a broad tendency toward lower WHR in many populations' is defensible, '0.7 is a universal constant' is not [ESTIMATE].

The male-attractiveness dimension pairing with female WHR in cross-cultural preference research (Plymouth PEARL) [FACT]; Frederick & Haselton (2007) found an inverted-U where MODERATE (not maximal) muscularity rates most attractive, with a methodological caveat that their drawings/CGI figures may bias the optimum toward supra-normal strength [FACT, contested]; PMC5745404 finds upper-body-strength cues explain most of the variance in men's rated bodily attractiveness [FACT].

Dunn & Searle (2010, British Journal of Psychology 101:69-80, doi:10.1348/000712609X417319): the same male model was rated significantly more attractive by female raters in a prestige car (Bentley) vs a neutral car (Fiesta), while the same female model's ratings by male raters did not differ by car [FACT]; a 2023 replication supports the status-attractiveness link generally [FACT]; treated here as a working hypothesis from one experimental paradigm, not settled law [ESTIMATE].

Grabe, Ward & Hyde (2008, Psychological Bulletin 134:460-476), a meta-analysis of 77 studies/141 effect sizes: exposure to ultra-thin media ideals is associated with increased body dissatisfaction, thin-ideal internalization, and disordered-eating beliefs in women, with small-to-moderate mean effect sizes (d approx -0.28, -0.39, -0.30) [FACT]; this is the ethical basis, independent of platform rules, for holding an aspirational-not-degrading line [ESTIMATE].

Two distinct persuasion levers this KB keeps separate: aspiration (the audience wants to BECOME or possess what the persona has, driving luxury/status content per Dunn & Searle) and identification/self-congruity (the audience sees an ideal self in the persona, driving parasocial trust per Horton & Wohl 1956 and Han et al. 2024's finding that Source Credibility Theory is the most robust explanatory framework, with Parasocial Interaction and Congruity Theory also significant) [FACT, framing ESTIMATE].

The orchestrator's binding commitment [ESTIMATE]: attractiveness is delivered via styling, silhouette, tailoring, status context, expression, and cinematography -- never via nudity, sexualized posing, or solicitation -- because the A2 research (status cues, V-taper, WHR-flattering silhouette, face/gaze craft) shows this is sufficient to do the attraction work without tripping the Instagram taste floor or the A2.4 harm evidence.

The core right-of-publicity doctrine: the protected interest is IDENTIFIABILITY of a real person, established through ANY cue -- face, look-alike appearance (Onassis v. Christian Dior, 1984), voice alone (Midler v. Ford, 849 F.2d 460, 9th Cir. 1988), or context/associated objects with no depiction of the person at all (White v. Samsung, 971 F.2d 1395, 9th Cir. 1992) [FACT]. Hiding the face does not remove liability because the face was never the sole trigger.

The buildable alternative [ESTIMATE, legally reasoned]: deliver the visual GRAMMAR of fame (paparazzi flash/long-lens framing, entourage/bodyguard staging, red-carpet/backstage framing with an invented sponsor wall) attached to wholly FICTIONAL, self-contained personas with their own invented name/backstory/brand/press -- never a real person's identity, name-adjacent cue, or look-alike casting.

nodes.definition: Establish the face-first fixation finding as the composition anchor for any persona frame. Cerf, Frady & Koch (Journal of Vision, 2009) tracked eye movements in free-viewing and search tasks and found adults fixate faces preferentially and largely independent of task; adding a face-detection channel (Viola-Jones) to a bottom-up Itti-Koch saliency model raised fixation-prediction AUC to >0.84 versus ~0.53 for the classic bottom-up model alone on natural scenes [FACT]. The pattern replicates on real-world stimulus materials (ACM ETRA 2020) [FACT]. Practical craft read [ESTIMATE, high confidence]: in a 3-6 second reel frame, a human face is the near-certain first-fixation anchor, so the face should be placed where attention should START, with composition/motion handing attention off to product or setting afterward.

included: Cerf/Frady/Koch 2009 fixation-prediction AUC result
the ACM ETRA 2020 real-world replication
the face-as-first-fixation-anchor composition rule
excluded: gaze-direction effects on downstream memory/purchase (its own node)
motion/contrast salience mechanics (its own node)

pros.claim: Placing the face as the deliberate first-fixation anchor lets a shot's composition control where attention starts before handing off
pros.example: opening a frame face-forward then using a hand gesture or product motion to carry the eye onward, matching the Cerf et al. fixation-prediction result

cons.claim: Over-relying on face salience without a deliberate handoff leaves the viewer's eye anchored on the face and the product/setting under-attended
cons.example: a static face-only close-up that never cues the eye toward the product, wasting the frame's persuasive intent

failure_modes: treating face-salience as guaranteeing product attention without a deliberate handoff cue
assuming the finding transfers to non-natural or heavily stylized imagery without caveat
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites the Cerf/Frady/Koch AUC result (>0.84 vs ~0.53) and the ETRA 2020 replication, and states the face-first-then-handoff composition rule
revisit_triggers: a new eye-tracking study changes the face-salience effect size
a stylized (non-photoreal) persona format is tested for whether the finding still transfers
the handoff cue is found not to redirect attention in practice

base.update_signal: a new fixation-prediction study or stylized-imagery test changes the transfer confidence

nodes.definition: Handle gaze-direction craft honestly: the literature is REAL but CONTESTED on magnitude and even direction. Gaze cueing -- observers shift attention toward where a depicted face looks -- is a robust basic-attention phenomenon (Frontiers in Psychology 2017, PMC5454066) [FACT, but the PMC body was 403-blocked this session so its specific effect sizes are UNKNOWN pending fetch]. Sajjacholapunt & Ball (2014, PMC3941030) found AVERTED gaze (toward the ad content) improved attention/memory outcomes [FACT]. But a ResearchGate-hosted eye-tracking study reports face + gaze DIRECTED TOWARD the product strongly influenced attention, memorization, ad/brand evaluation and purchase intention [FACT], and D'Ambrogio et al. (2023, Psychology & Marketing) show gaze direction interacts with celebrity status [FACT]. These directly conflict on which gaze convention wins. Honest synthesis [ESTIMATE, medium confidence]: gaze cueing moves attention reliably; whether gaze-to-product or gaze-to-viewer wins on memory/purchase depends on goal and context. Do not hard-code 'always look at the product' -- treat gaze direction as a per-shot A/B variable.

included: the gaze-cueing attention-shift phenomenon
the Sajjacholapunt-vs-ResearchGate/D'Ambrogio conflict on downstream outcomes
the per-shot A/B-variable framing
excluded: face-first fixation itself (its own node)
the specific status-prop interaction mechanics (its own node)

pros.claim: Treating gaze direction as an A/B variable avoids hard-coding a rule the literature itself disputes
pros.example: shooting both an averted-gaze and a product-directed-gaze take of the same frame and testing which performs for a given persona/context

cons.claim: Refusing to commit to a single gaze rule adds production overhead (two takes/variants) versus a simple fixed convention
cons.example: a small production run that cannot afford to shoot and test both gaze variants and must guess

failure_modes: hard-coding 'gaze must point at the product' as if the literature were settled
citing PMC5454066's specific effect sizes as fetched fact when the body was 403-blocked
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the Sajjacholapunt averted-gaze finding and the ResearchGate/D'Ambrogio gaze-to-product findings as being in direct conflict, states the PMC5454066 UNKNOWN-effect-size caveat, and recommends per-shot A/B testing over a fixed rule
revisit_triggers: the PMC5454066 body becomes fetchable and the effect sizes can be verified
a persona-specific A/B test resolves which gaze convention wins for that context
a new study clarifies the gaze-direction/celebrity-status interaction

base.update_signal: the blocked PMC source becomes fetchable or an A/B test result resolves the contested direction

nodes.definition: Ground the motion/contrast craft rule in bottom-up saliency theory. The Itti-Koch lineage of bottom-up saliency models predicts fixations from low-level features -- luminance/color contrast, orientation, and especially motion/flicker are strong salience channels [FACT]; this is exactly the substrate Cerf et al. (2009) built their face-channel addition on top of, and its empirical fixation-prediction success supports the underlying bottom-up theory [FACT]. Craft translation [ESTIMATE, high confidence]: a single moving element against a still field (a car door opening, hair moving, fabric catching wind) is a reliable attention magnet; competing motion everywhere destroys the cue, and high local contrast on the intended focal point achieves the same effect in a still frame.

included: the Itti-Koch bottom-up saliency substrate and its motion/contrast channels
the single-moving-element-against-a-still-field craft rule
the competing-motion-destroys-the-cue failure mode
excluded: the face-channel addition on top of this substrate (its own node)
gaze-direction effects (its own node)

pros.claim: A single deliberate motion cue against an otherwise still frame reliably captures and directs attention without needing a face
pros.example: a slow hair-flutter or fabric movement as the sole moving element in an otherwise static luxury-setting frame

cons.claim: Multiple competing motion sources in one frame cancel the salience advantage entirely
cons.example: background crowd motion, camera shake, and subject motion all present at once leaving no single fixation anchor

failure_modes: stacking multiple simultaneous motion cues and destroying the single-magnet effect
assuming a still frame needs no contrast design because 'the face will be looked at anyway'
acceptance_tests: the analysis grounds the rule in Itti-Koch bottom-up saliency and Cerf et al.'s substrate, and states the single-moving-element/still-field rule with the competing-motion failure mode
revisit_triggers: a frame with multiple motion sources is found to underperform in review
a still-frame contrast-design choice is tested against a control

base.update_signal: a multi-motion frame underperforms or a new saliency-model result changes the weighting

nodes.definition: State what the WHR research supports and where it breaks. Singh (1993) reported a lower waist-to-hip ratio (~0.7) and moderate body weight rated more attractive for female figures across observers [FACT]. Tassinary & Hansen (1998) criticized Singh's line-drawing stimuli for confounding WHR with waist size and body weight, built 27 unconfounded stimuli, and got complicating results; Henss (1995) replicated with somewhat different results; cross-cultural work is mixed, with one study finding Ugandan raters preferred ~0.5 WHR and heavier weight [FACT, contested]. Honest read [ESTIMATE, medium confidence]: 'a broad tendency toward lower WHR for female attractiveness in many populations' is defensible; '0.7 is a universal constant' is NOT -- weight, culture, and stimulus artifacts move it. Craft target: silhouette/tailoring reading as WHR-flattering cut, never explicit exposure, per the aspirational-not-explicit house rule.

included: Singh 1993's ~0.7 WHR finding and the Tassinary & Hansen confound critique
the Ugandan cross-cultural outlier
the 'broad tendency, not universal constant' honest read
excluded: male shoulder-to-hip/V-taper research (its own node)
explicit-exposure styling, which is out of scope per the house rule

pros.claim: Naming the WHR tendency as broad-but-culturally-variable, not a fixed constant, prevents over-committing styling to a disputed number
pros.example: tailoring a silhouette to read 'WHR-flattering' in a general sense rather than engineering an exact 0.7 ratio

cons.claim: The confound critique and cross-cultural mixed results mean there is no single safe numeric target to hand a stylist
cons.example: a stylist asking for an exact target ratio and receiving only a qualitative direction because the literature does not support a precise universal number

failure_modes: quoting Singh's 0.7 as a universal, uncontested constant
ignoring the Tassinary & Hansen confound critique or the cross-cultural outlier when briefing styling
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites Singh 1993's ~0.7 finding, the Tassinary & Hansen confound critique, the Ugandan ~0.5 outlier, and states the tendency-not-constant conclusion
revisit_triggers: a new cross-cultural WHR study is published
a styling brief asks for an exact numeric WHR target that the literature cannot support
the confound critique is itself re-examined by newer methodology

base.update_signal: a new cross-cultural WHR study or a request for an unsupported precise target surfaces

nodes.definition: State what the male-physique research supports. Frederick & Haselton (2007, PSPB), across six studies, found MODERATE muscularity rated most attractive -- an inverted-U, not 'more is better'; women rated more-muscular men sexier and more physically dominant but less committed as long-term mates [FACT]. A methodological caveat from the authors' critics: the study used drawings/CGI male figures, some at supra-normal strength, which may bias the 'moderate' optimum [FACT, contested]. Later work (PMC5745404) finds upper-body-strength cues explain a large share of variance in men's rated bodily attractiveness [FACT]. Cross-cultural preference research pairs women's WHR with men's shoulder-to-hip ratio (V-taper) as complementary dimorphism cues (Plymouth PEARL) [FACT]. Craft read [ESTIMATE, medium confidence]: a V-taper / evident-but-not-extreme upper-body-strength cue is the supported target, NOT maximal bodybuilder mass.

included: Frederick & Haselton's inverted-U moderate-muscularity finding and its supra-normal-stimulus caveat
the upper-body-strength-variance result (PMC5745404)
the V-taper craft target vs maximal mass
excluded: female WHR research (its own node)
the status-prop asymmetry that pairs with physique styling (its own node)

pros.claim: Targeting moderate V-taper rather than maximal mass matches the actual inverted-U finding instead of an assumed 'bigger is better' heuristic
pros.example: styling/casting toward an evident-but-not-extreme upper-body silhouette rather than a bodybuilder physique

cons.claim: The supra-normal-stimulus caveat means the 'moderate' optimum itself may be biased by the original study's drawings/CGI, so the exact optimum is uncertain
cons.example: treating Frederick & Haselton's specific moderate point as precisely calibrated when their own critics flag the stimuli as biased

failure_modes: defaulting to maximal muscularity on a 'more attractive = more muscular' assumption the inverted-U contradicts
ignoring the supra-normal-stimulus caveat when citing the 'moderate' finding as precise
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites the Frederick & Haselton inverted-U finding with its caveat, the PMC5745404 upper-body-strength result, and states the V-taper-not-maximal-mass craft target
revisit_triggers: a new muscularity-attractiveness study using non-drawn stimuli is published
a casting/styling brief defaults to maximal mass against this finding
the upper-body-strength-variance result is extended or challenged

base.update_signal: a non-drawn-stimuli replication or a maximal-mass casting brief surfaces

nodes.definition: State the one experimental result on status-prop asymmetry precisely. Dunn & Searle (British Journal of Psychology, 2010, 101:69-80, doi:10.1348/000712609X417319): the same models, same expression/posture, were seated in a high-status car (silver Bentley Continental GT) vs a neutral car (red Ford Fiesta ST). Result: the MALE target was rated significantly more attractive by female raters in the high-status car; the FEMALE target's ratings by male raters did NOT differ by car [FACT]. A 2023 replication/extension ('Luxurious cars increase perceptions of status, social dominance, and attractiveness') supports the general status-attractiveness link [FACT]. Read [ESTIMATE, medium-high confidence]: luxury-status props (car, watch, setting) plausibly lift the MALE persona's attractiveness signal to a female audience more than they lift the FEMALE persona's to a male audience -- but this is one experimental paradigm, treated as a working hypothesis, not law.

included: the exact Dunn & Searle 2010 Bentley-vs-Fiesta result and citation
the 2023 replication supporting the general status-attractiveness link
the working-hypothesis-not-law framing
excluded: the aspiration/identification framing this result feeds into (its own node)
styling-prop sourcing logistics (belongs to the luxury specialist)

pros.claim: Naming the asymmetry precisely lets status props be deployed where the evidence says they work hardest -- the male persona's female-facing appeal
pros.example: prioritizing a high-status vehicle/setting prop for the male persona's female-audience content over the female persona's male-audience content

cons.claim: Generalizing from one experimental paradigm (two specific cars, one study population) to a hard rule risks overfitting to that paradigm
cons.example: assuming the asymmetry holds for every luxury-prop category and every audience culture without further testing

failure_modes: treating the Dunn & Searle result as a universal law rather than one paradigm's finding
applying the asymmetry to the female persona's styling as if it also lifted her opposite-sex ratings
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites the exact Dunn & Searle 2010 citation and result (male lift, no female-side shift) and the 2023 replication, and frames it as a working hypothesis
revisit_triggers: a replication using different status props or populations is published
a persona's actual performance data contradicts the asymmetry
the working hypothesis is escalated or downgraded by new evidence

base.update_signal: a new status-prop replication or contradicting performance data surfaces

nodes.definition: State the documented downside of idealized imagery that must inform taste, independent of platform rules. Grabe, Ward & Hyde (2008, Psychological Bulletin 134:460-476), a meta-analysis of 77 studies / 141 effect sizes: exposure to media depicting ultra-thin ideals was associated with increased body dissatisfaction, thin-ideal internalization, and disordered-eating beliefs in women; mean effect sizes small-to-moderate (d approx -0.28, -0.39, -0.30) [FACT]. Implication [ESTIMATE, high confidence]: idealized imagery works on attention and aspiration AND measurably harms a slice of the audience -- this is the ethical/brand reason to hold the aspirational-not-degrading line, independent of the Instagram taste-floor policy.

included: the Grabe/Ward/Hyde 2008 meta-analysis (77 studies/141 effect sizes, d approx -0.28/-0.39/-0.30)
the ethical (not just policy) basis for the aspirational line
the harm applying specifically to idealized-thin-ideal exposure in women
excluded: the Instagram policy floor itself (its own node)
the house rule's operational content (its own node)

pros.claim: Grounding the aspirational-not-explicit line in measured harm, not just platform policy, gives it an ethical foundation that survives a policy change
pros.example: holding the aspirational-not-degrading line even in a hypothetical platform with looser nudity rules, because the harm evidence is independent of policy

cons.claim: A meta-analytic small-to-moderate effect size does not by itself dictate a specific styling decision, so translating it into concrete craft rules still requires judgment

nodes.definition: Define the safe lane the specialists CAN deliver [ESTIMATE, high confidence, legally reasoned]: celebrity-CODED aesthetics with FICTIONAL/anonymous figures pointing at NO specific real person. The visual GRAMMAR of fame is not owned by anyone; a specific person's identity is. Buildable elements: paparazzi visual grammar (flash falloff, long-lens compression, caught-candid framing, motion blur, crowd-edge composition -- genre, not identity); entourage/bodyguard staging (generic dark-suited silhouettes, earpiece, formation walking -- archetypes, not real security details); red-carpet/backstage/step-and-repeat framing with a FICTIONAL sponsor wall (invented brand/logo, never a real event's marks); fictional-fame worldbuilding giving each persona their OWN invented name, backstory, invented brand associations, invented press. Hard constraint: no real logos, no real event names, no real associated objects tied to a specific living/dead person, no name-adjacent cues, no look-alike casting of a specific person's silhouette/hair/style.

nodes.definition: Compose the operational stop-or-ship checklist an expert must run before any celebrity-coded output. (1) Is any REAL, specific person identifiable by ANY cue -- face, silhouette, hair, voice, styling, associated object, setting, name, initials, or name-adjacent hint? If yes, STOP; redesign or kill. (2) Does the content imply a real person's presence, association, or endorsement? If yes, STOP (right of publicity + FTC). (3) Are all logos/venues/events/brands FICTIONAL/invented? If no, replace. (4) Is the persona's fame self-contained fictional worldbuilding (own name/backstory)? If no, fix. (5) Is the output labeled/disclosed as AI-generated per Meta policy? If no, add disclosure. (6) Does it clear the taste floor (aspirational-not-explicit, no nudity/solicitation)? If no, restyle. Only if items 1-2 are firmly NO and items 3-6 are YES does the content ship [FACT-derived operational checklist].

nodes.definition: State the closed lane plainly, as the final word this KB gives on the owner's original premise. The owner's premise -- make composite images evoking famous people while 'not revealing the face, so it's safe' -- is legally wrong. Hiding the face does NOT make an identifiable-person implication safe: Onassis (look-alike, face shown but not the real person), Midler (voice only), and White (a robot + context, no person depicted at all) each found liability or a triable claim with no reliance on the real person's actual face [FACT-grounded conclusion]. This KB gives the true boundary and the safe fictional lane -- it does NOT give guidance for maximizing deniability while still evoking a specific real person. That lane is CLOSED. The verdict to relay plainly: the plan risks (a) state right-of-publicity liability including common-law evocation, (b) the emerging AI-likeness statutes, (c) Meta impersonation/deception enforcement, and (d) FTC deceptive-endorsement exposure -- face-hiding changes none of that.

excluded: the safe fictional lane this closed lane is contrasted against (its own node)

anti_rework_rules.prevents: producing a full shoot around a face-hidden real-person-evocation concept that must be scrapped once the doctrine is applied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the fictional-persona name/backstory/worldbuilding before any styling or staging begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: styling a shoot around a real-celebrity-adjacent concept that later has to be retrofitted with invented worldbuilding once the closed lane is invoked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm all logos/venues/sponsor walls are invented before set/prop sourcing begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sourcing or building real-brand set dressing that must be re-built as fictional after a legal review flags the associated-object risk

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat gaze direction as a per-shot decision recorded at brief time, not resolved during editing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shooting only one gaze convention and discovering in edit that the contested evidence calls for testing the other, requiring a reshoot

anti_rework_rules.rule: Flag any borderline taste-floor styling call for a live Instagram-policy re-fetch before shooting, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shooting content against an assumed policy threshold that a later live-policy check finds non-compliant, forcing a reshoot

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the AI-likeness statute cluster and FTC/Meta regulatory layer before any AI voice or likeness asset is generated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: generating a voice/likeness asset that must be discarded and regenerated once a statutory or regulatory check is finally run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the full six-item stop-checklist at concept approval, not only at final review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering an identifiability or fictional-constraint failure only at final review, after styling, staging, and production work has already been completed

iteration_protocol.trigger: the proxy block on transparency.meta.com or pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov clears
iteration_protocol.action: re-fetch the Instagram policy pages and the PMC5454066 gaze-cuing body directly, and upgrade the affected claims from indexed-summary to fetched-fact confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new state enacts an AI-likeness/digital-replica statute, or a federal NO-FAKES-style act's status becomes verifiable
iteration_protocol.action: add the new statute to the AI-likeness statute cluster with its exact citation and effective date, and re-run the stop-checklist's statutory-clearance step against it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new right-of-publicity case narrows or broadens the appropriation/evocation doctrinal split
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine the identifiability-not-face doctrine and each of the three precedent nodes against the new case's holding

iteration_protocol.trigger: a persona's actual content performance data becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: test the status-prop asymmetry and the aspiration-vs-identification lever split against real engagement data rather than relying solely on the cited studies

iteration_protocol.trigger: Meta updates the Adult Nudity/Solicitation standard, the Authentic Identity Representation standard, or the AI-labeling policy
iteration_protocol.action: re-fetch and re-state the affected policy nodes, re-checking the aspirational-not-explicit house rule and safe-lane hard constraints against the update

iteration_protocol.trigger: a production proposes a new celebrity-coded concept not yet covered by the safe lane's four buildable elements
iteration_protocol.action: extend the safe-lane definition with the new element only if it passes the fictional-only hard constraint, then re-run the stop-checklist

iteration_protocol.trigger: the FTC revises the Endorsement Guides or the 'significant minority' disclosure threshold
iteration_protocol.action: re-state the FTC node's threshold and re-check any implied-association content against the revised standard

priority_rationale: The A1-A3 psychology foundations (face fixation, gaze, motion, WHR, V-taper, status props, harm evidence, aspiration/identification) come first because the craft table and the house rule are read against them; the composed craft table and the taste-floor/house-rule nodes come next because they bound what the psychology permits; the three law precedents and the identifiability doctrine follow as the load-bearing legal foundation everything downstream must satisfy; the state and AI-specific statutes, then the FTC/Meta regulatory layer, extend that doctrine into concrete remedies and platform obligations; and the safe lane, the stop-checklist, and the closed-lane statement come last because they synthesize every upstream psychology, taste, and law node into the one operational verdict a specialist must apply before any output ships.
